rationale: Start with a broad, mid-temperature scouting gradient to elute all 10 compounds and reveal the overall retention window without an excessive risk of truncation. The wide composition range and moderate slope should give an informative first map of spacing across the chromatogram.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the next move is to reduce analysis time while keeping selectivity essentially unchanged. Shortening the gradient at the same composition window and temperature should pull the last peak closer to 10 min and test how much time margin we really have.

We are very close to the ideal 10 min endpoint and the limiting pair still has slight resolution margin, so one more step shorter is the most efficient test. This should show whether we can eliminate the remaining time penalty without pushing the weakest pair below full-credit resolution.

At 14 min the only loss is the 6/7 pair, so keep the faster gradient and adjust selectivity rather than slowing the method again. Dropping temperature one step often increases retention and can improve marginal resolution enough to recover full credit while staying under the 10 min last-peak target.

Lowering temperature hurt selectivity, so test the opposite direction while keeping the faster 14 min gradient that already meets the time target. A 5 C increase may improve the critical spacing near peaks 5–7 and 6–7 enough to reach full resolution without reintroducing a time penalty.

Temperature changes worsened the critical region, so keep the favorable 40 C selectivity and instead slightly narrow the gradient window at the strong end to reduce late-elution compression. Lowering phi1 by one step may preserve the sub-10 min endpoint while giving peaks 5–7 a bit more spacing.

Lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the limiting 6/7 pair while keeping t_last under 10 min, so continue one more step in the same direction. This is the most direct test for reaching full resolution credit at essentially the same optimal run time.

At phi1 0.85 all pairs now have full-credit resolution, so the next step is to shorten the method until the critical pair just begins to fail. Reducing tG by one step should cut t_last back toward 10 min and may improve the CRF if resolution stays at or above 1.5.

At tG 12, phi1 0.85 was too compressed around the critical 6/7 pair, while phi1 0.90 at tG 14 was close to full credit and still under 10 min. Testing phi1 0.90 with the shorter gradient checks whether a slightly wider window restores enough spacing to beat the current best.

The best point so far is very close to ideal, and the main unmet goal is pushing the 6/7 pair from 1.36 to at least 1.5 while staying near 10 min. Since shortening tG hurt that pair and lowering phi1 helped it, a slightly longer gradient at phi1 0.90 is the most promising way to gain the remaining resolution credit with only a small time penalty.

The optimum appears to lie between the fully resolved but slightly slow method (0.05/0.85/14) and the faster but slightly under-resolved one (0.05/0.90/14). Raising phi0 one step while keeping phi1 0.85 and tG 14 should compress the early part, potentially trimming t_last below 10 min while preserving the favorable selectivity that gave full resolution.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so the only remaining objective is to see whether a still shorter effective retention window can preserve full resolution while pulling the last peak just under 10 min. Increasing phi0 one more step is the cleanest local refinement around the optimum without changing the successful selectivity pattern too drastically.

The last change improved t_last while maintaining full-credit resolution, so continue stepping phi0 upward to locate the shortest fully resolved boundary. This tests whether we can keep all pairs at or above 1.5 while further reducing total retention.

Phi0 0.20 was too aggressive and cost resolution on the 6/7 pair, so return to the successful phi0 0.15 and tighten the high-organic endpoint instead. Lowering phi1 by one step should recover or improve the critical spacing while likely keeping the last peak comfortably under 10 min.

The current optimum is already at the maximum score, so the remaining useful search is to see whether the successful phi0 0.15 / phi1 0.85 window can tolerate a shorter gradient. This directly tests whether we can keep full resolution while further reducing run time around the best region.

Both 0.10/0.85/14 and 0.15/0.85/14 reached CRF 1.000, while 0.15/0.80/14 was fully resolved but slightly too slow. Testing 0.10/0.80/14 probes the missing corner of this optimal region and may combine the stronger 0.80-end selectivity with a slightly shorter last-peak time.

The best region is centered at phi0 0.10–0.15 and phi1 0.85, and phi0 0.15 gave the shortest fully resolved run so far. Testing phi1 0.90 at the same phi0 checks the other neighboring corner of that local optimum to confirm whether 0.85 is truly best or if a slightly wider window can retain full resolution with similar timing.

The composition optimum is already established, so the only plausible improvement path left is a small temperature tweak around a max-score method. Testing 45 C on the 0.10/0.85/14 condition checks whether the 6/7 pair can remain fully resolved while nudging the last peak just below 10 min.

Since raising temperature badly collapsed the critical 6/7 pair, test the opposite direction once on the proven max-score composition to complete the local temperature map. If 35 C preserves full resolution and slightly lengthens retention, it could still remain at CRF 1.000 and confirm 40 C as the true optimum or reveal a second equally good setting.

Temperature is clearly suboptimal away from 40 C, so return to the best composition region and map the slower side of tG at the best-scoring phi0 0.15. This checks whether there is any extra robustness margin in the critical pair and confirms that 14 min is the shortest fully resolved setting around the optimum.

We already know two max-score solutions at phi1 0.85, and the remaining untested nearby point is phi0 0.10 / phi1 0.90 at the same tG and temperature. This completes the local response surface around the optimum and checks whether a slightly wider gradient window can still keep all pairs resolved with no time penalty.

The two 14 min methods at phi1 0.85 are optimal, but phi0 0.10 has slightly more margin on the critical 6/7 pair than phi0 0.15. Testing the shorter 12 min gradient here checks whether that extra margin is enough to preserve full resolution and uncover a faster equally optimal method.

The optimum is already established, so with the remaining budget it is reasonable to probe whether a strong temperature decrease creates an alternative selectivity pattern around the same composition window. This may reveal whether the critical pair can be improved enough to stay fully resolved while still keeping retention acceptable, though 40 C remains the benchmark.

With the optimum already secured, use one of the final injections to complete the nearby composition map at 40 C by testing the untried corner phi0 0.20 / phi1 0.90. This will show whether the loss seen at phi0 0.20 is mainly driven by high phi0 itself or whether a wider gradient window compensates the critical 6/7 separation.

For the final shot, target the only remaining plausible faster fully resolved region by combining the stronger 0.80 endpoint selectivity with the more favorable phi0 0.15 and shorter tG 12. This tests whether the extra resolution margin seen at 0.15/0.80/14 can survive a shorter gradient and reveal another max-score method.
